QF.id: VB Fund Distribution and Channel Management_29

question.text: When a mutual fund distributor (MFD) passes away, commission is paid to the nominee or legal heirs. Regarding the nominee's eligibility, __________.

answer.text: The nominee need not be an ARN holder to receive commission
The nominee must be a registered ARN holder
The nominee must hold a valid NISM certification
The nominee must be registered with SEBI as a distributor

explanation.text: The Logic: To simply receive commission on the deceased MFD's existing assets, the nominee or legal heir need not be an ARN holder — the workbook directly supports this entitlement. The Trap: Receiving commission must be distinguished from conducting new business or transferring the AUM. No new business can be solicited under the deceased MFD's ARN code, and any transfer of AUM to the nominee/legal heir requires that person to hold a valid ARN and meet KYD/self-certification conditions, with trustee approval and the assets remaining valid. Note: The "no ARN needed" rule applies narrowly to receiving commission; it should not be read as a blanket waiver of registration for taking over the distribution business or assets.
